area_workshop_about: Make learning views and visualizations with an agent; publish them to a class, or offer them for the public site.
area_review_about: What the workshops offered for the public site: accept or reject it.
area_runs_about: Every agent turn: what it was sent, what it did, its time, tokens, cost and rating.
viz_brief_placeholder: e.g. Show how a Bézier curve is drawn by de Casteljau's construction; the control points are draggable.

match.n=one: This browser keeps {count} draft from the workshops before they moved to accounts. Move it to your account?
match.n=other: This browser keeps {count} drafts from the workshops before they moved to accounts. Move them to your account?

move_once: They stay here too. You’re asked once.
submit_title: Offer it for the public site
submit_about: Offer this for the public site, where anyone can use it for free. It’s reviewed first, and may be changed.
signed_out: You were signed out: reload the page and sign in again.
submit_what: What it is, for someone looking for it
submit_credit: Credit it to (optional, shown with it)
submit_rights: I made this, or may share it, and agree that it’s published under {licence}.
login_mismatch: That email and password don’t match.
kind_view_ask: What will it be? A title; you describe it in the chat next.
kind_viz_ask: What will it be? A title; you write its spec next.
kind_sequence_ask: What will the lesson be? A title; you put its steps together next.
agent_working: The agent is working on it
drafts_none: Nothing yet: make a view, a visualization, or a lesson of several views.
drafts_pick: Pick a draft, or make a new one.
view_brief_placeholder: What should it be? Who is it for, what do they do in it, what should they get out of it?
publish_off_confirm: Switch the link off? Students who open it see that it isn’t available. Publishing again switches it back on.
publish_link: Students open it with this link. It works without an account; anyone who has it can open it.
publish_revoked: The link is switched off. Publishing switches it on again.
publish_about: Publishing makes a link for your students. What they do in the lesson stays on their device.
publish_not_ready_agent: It wasn’t published: it isn’t ready yet. Ask the agent in the chat to fix this (you can paste it):
publish_not_ready: It wasn’t published: it isn’t ready yet.
download: Download it, as a folder in a zip
delete_confirm: Delete “{title}”? A link you published keeps working until you switch it off.
claude_bridge_ok: The bridge is there, finds Claude Code, and lets this site use it.
claude_bridge_start: Install the Claude bridge and Claude Code on this computer, then start the bridge
ollama_bridge_ok: The bridge is there, Ollama has the model, and the bridge lets this site use it.
ollama_bridge_start: Install Ollama and start the Ollama bridge on this computer (mise run ollama-bridge)
agent_cli_about: The {command} command you’re signed in to here, on your own plan, through the Claude bridge.
agent_ollama_about: A local model, through the Ollama bridge. Free, and much weaker than Claude.
agent_gemini_about: Google’s free models on your own AI Studio key, called from this browser; the conversation stays in this tab. Google may use what’s sent on the free tier to improve its products.
settings_agents: Who makes views and plans lessons with you
settings_agents_order: Tried from the top: the first one switched on that’s ready takes the turn.
gemini_make: Make one, free, here (it’s kept in this browser and sent only to Google):
bridge_asks: {start}. It asks you once, on this computer, whether this site may use it. Your browser may ask too, whether this site may use apps on this device.
seq_about: Each step is one of your views or visualizations, played in order. A step may be skipped when the student already knows something, or get an extra view first when they struggle with it. Make them first, as drafts of their own.
seq_no_views: You have no views or visualizations yet: make one with New first.
plan_placeholder: What should the lesson do, for whom? e.g. Year 2: adding across ten up to 100; those who can already do it shouldn’t be bored.
plan_one_view: The agent thinks this is one view, not several: {why} Make it with New → View.
plan_detour: extra first if they struggle with {concept}: {title}

match.n=one: Taking it makes {count} draft, with its brief kept with it. It is built when you ask its chat to.
match.n=other: Taking it makes {count} drafts, each with its brief kept with it. Each is built when you ask its chat to, one at a time: start with the first, and see if it’s what you want before the others.

plan_made: Made {titles}. Open each from the list to build it; until they’re built, the check below misses the concepts they’ll practise.
rule_detour: Extra view first if they struggle with
play_new: is new to all of it
sign_in_first: Sign in at the workshop first:
review_rejected: Rejected; the sender sees your note.
review_accepted_into: Accepted into {path}. It goes public once it’s committed and the site is built:
review_as_package: Its gestalts in the package gestalts/…
review_concepts: What it practises as a whole: concept names in English, comma-separated (outlines find it by these)
review_into_checkout: Into {path}, to be checked and committed there.
review_no_checkout: This server accepts into no checkout (start it with --promote-into): only rejecting works here.
